Telecommunications Workers Strike Disrupts Services Across Uzbekistan

A widespread walkout by telecommunications workers disrupted services across Uzbekistan on Tuesday, as hundreds of employees from major providers, including Uzbektelecom JSC, staged a coordinated strike over pay and working conditions. The industrial action, which began early in the morning, has affected both fixed-line and mobile services in several regions, according to industry sources.

Customers in Tashkent and other major cities reported disruptions to internet and telephone connectivity, with some users experiencing intermittent outages and slower data speeds. Uzbektelecom JSC confirmed in a statement that the company was "working to minimize service interruptions" and was "actively engaging with employee representatives to resolve the situation as quickly as possible."

According to the National Telecommunications Workers’ Union, more than 2,000 employees across the sector participated in the walkout. “Our members are seeking fair wages and better job security,” said union spokesperson Dilshod Yuldashev. “We regret the inconvenience to customers, but our demands have not been addressed for months.”

Industry analysts estimate that service disruptions could impact up to 20 percent of the country’s telecommunications traffic if the strike continues. “Uzbekistan’s growing reliance on digital services means any prolonged disruption will have significant consequences for business and daily life,” said Saida Rakhimova, an independent telecoms analyst based in Tashkent.

FayzNet, another major operator, reported delays in customer support and maintenance activities. The Uzbekistan Association of Telecommunications Operators urged all parties to “return to negotiations and restore normal service as soon as possible.”

As of Tuesday afternoon, talks between union leaders and management had yet to produce a resolution, and services remained affected in several regions. The union has indicated that the strike will continue until their demands are met, raising concerns about further disruptions in the days ahead.
